  • Core 1 centres on financial accounting and reporting. Together the two core modules build breadth across the technical areas and draw on law, economics, finance, strategy, statistics and IT. A10W22

  • Candidates who miss the workshop cannot write the exam. W22

blocks.ostepAll:
All 8 steps

Step 1 · Before you start

Entry: a degree, 120 credit hours and 14 prerequisite courses

  • A degree and 120 credit hours of post-secondary education, plus 14 prerequisite courses: nine core and five non-core. W27W30
  • Grades: at least 60% in each core course, 50% in each non-core course, and a 65% average across the core courses. W27ON18ON19
  • Missing prerequisites can be taken at a post-secondary institution, through the profession’s own preparatory courses, or a mix of both. W27ON19
  • Preparatory courses are not part of the certification program itself; they exist to fill prerequisite gaps. W33
OntarioCPA Ontario runs its own preparatory courses (PREP). A four-year degree, or 120 credit hours, is required. The last PREP exam is December 2026. ON19ON18ON14
QuebecEntry is through a bachelor’s degree, then either a university graduate program (minimum average 2.8/4.3, set by each university) or the National Program delivered by the Order. QC16QC18
WestCPAWSB preparatory courses cover all 14 prerequisites; at least one core course per competency area must be within 10 years. Applicants without a degree can use an eight-year “mature status” route. Courses end December 2027. W27W30
AtlanticCPA Atlantic preparatory courses cost $850 per core course and $655 per non-core course and run until December 2027. Applications to CPA PEP itself have closed. A11A10
Step 2 · Module 1

Core 1: financial accounting and reporting

  • Core 1 centres on financial accounting and reporting. Together the two core modules build breadth across the technical areas and draw on law, economics, finance, strategy, statistics and IT. A10W22
  • About eight weeks of online learning with weekly assignments, 15 to 20 hours of study a week, and a mandatory two-day workshop. A two-day orientation workshop precedes Core 1. W22W29
  • Ends with a four-hour, in-person exam of objective-format questions and short cases. CPA Canada sets the dates and marks every exam nationally. W28W29
  • Candidates who miss the workshop cannot write the exam. W22
OntarioModule fee $1,525 + HST. Exams are written at centres across Ontario. ON18ON20
QuebecNational Program: online modules with in-class workshops, exams at a centre in Montréal, and a coach for each group of 6 to 10. University students take equivalent courses instead. QC16QC17QC20
WestModule fee $1,630 + GST. Final session Jan 23 – Mar 24, 2027; last exam, rewrite only, Jun 30, 2027. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,910 + HST. A 20-week extended version was offered alongside the eight-week one. A10
Step 3 · Module 2

Core 2: management accounting, planning and control

  • Core 2 centres on management accounting, planning and control. A10
  • Same format as Core 1: about eight weeks online, a two-day workshop and a four-hour exam. W29W28
  • Core 1 must be completed before Core 2 unless the two are taken together on the fast-track pathway, which takes about 40 hours a week. W28W29
OntarioModule fee $1,450 + HST. Final Core 2 exam September 2027. ON18ON14
QuebecEach National Program module costs $1,747.62 with taxes. Last offering Jul 24 – Sep 17, 2027. QC19QC10
WestModule fee $1,470 + GST. Final session Jul 24 – Sep 22, 2027. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 4 · Modules 3 and 4

Two elective modules: the specialization choice

  • Candidates choose two of four: Assurance, Taxation, Finance and Performance Management. The focus is depth. W22
  • Both core modules must be complete before the electives. Each elective ends with its own four-hour exam. W29W28
  • Public accounting requires the Assurance and Taxation electives. W22ON21
  • The elective choice also shapes the CFE: Day 2 is written in one of four roles that mirror the electives. ON21W32
OntarioEach elective $1,450 + HST. Final elective exams March 2028. ON18ON14
QuebecGraduate-program students choose two of the four as university courses; the Assurance and Taxation courses are needed for the CPA auditor designation. QC16QC18
WestEach elective $1,470 + GST. Final session Jan 29 – Mar 29, 2028; all elective exams fall on the same day, so candidates are told to plan for one. W31W25
AtlanticEach elective $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 5 · Module 5

Capstone 1: the integrative team case

  • Teams work through one large business case, building strategic leadership, teamwork and communication skills. The same case is the basis of Day 1 of the CFE. W22W32
  • There is no exam. Candidates are evaluated on a group report and an oral presentation to a panel. W32QC17
  • Two electives must be passed before Capstone 1. W28
  • Each Capstone 1 case is used for two CFE sittings. W32
OntarioModule fee $1,450 + HST. Recommended immediately before the CFE: Capstone 1 from May for a September CFE. ON18ON17
QuebecAssessed on three components: individual contribution to teamwork, the group report and the oral presentation. Last offered spring 2028. QC17QC10
WestModule fee $1,470 + GST. Final offering May 27 – Jul 28, 2028, presentations Jul 21–27. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 6 · Module 6

Capstone 2: preparation for the Common Final Examination

  • Applies everything learned so far to complex, highly integrative practice cases. W22W32
  • No module exam. Candidates must complete a set number of practice cases to become eligible for the CFE. W32
  • Practice cases use the candidate’s declared elective role, the same role tested on Day 2 of the CFE. W32
OntarioModule fee $1,450 + HST. Recommended from July for a September CFE. ON18ON17
QuebecNo exam; once complete, the candidate can write the CFE. Last offered summer 2028. QC17QC10
WestModule fee $1,470 + GST. Final offering starts Aug 5, 2028. W31W25
AtlanticModule fee $1,595 + HST. A10
Step 7 · National exam

The Common Final Examination (CFE)

  • A three-day, 13-hour examination: Day 1 four hours, Day 2 five hours, Day 3 four hours. First-time writers must attempt all three days in the same sitting. W21W32
  • Day 1 is based on the Capstone 1 case. Day 2 tests depth in one of four elective roles together with Financial Reporting or Management Accounting. Day 3 tests breadth across all six technical areas. W32ON21ON22
  • Three attempts. Unlike module exams, the CFE cannot be deferred. QC17QC1W21
  • Only two sittings remain: Sep 8–10, 2027 and Sep 26–28, 2028. There are no May sittings. W25QC11
OntarioFee $2,050 + HST for all three days. Final CFE September 2028. ON18ON14
QuebecFee $1,997.12 with taxes. Written in French or English. QC19QC17
WestFee $2,070 + GST. First-attempt pass rate in 2025 was 69.8% (CPABC). W31BC1
AtlanticFee $1,940 + HST. A10
Step 8 · Finish

Membership: education, the CFE and practical experience

  • The certification program has three parts: CPA PEP, the CFE and 30 months of paid practical experience. W33BC1
  • Experience does not have to be finished before the CFE; it can be completed at any time within the program time limit. W16
  • A public accounting licence needs the Assurance and Taxation electives, the Assurance role on the CFE with depth in Assurance and Financial Reporting, and chargeable hours in audit or assurance. ON21
OntarioDeregistration deadlines: six years after starting CPA PEP unless the CFE has been attempted; seven years to finish experience; ten years after first registration. ON23
QuebecThe whole path must be completed within seven years of registering as a candidate. Practical experience is 24 months. QC16QC9
WestSix years for CPA PEP and seven years overall, with up to 24 months of approved leave. W23
AtlanticUp to six years for CPA PEP and the CFE. A10

blocks.opaths:
Graduate diploma in the summer, then a firm

The most common Ontario design. A 12 to 14-week diploma after graduation covers Core 1, Core 2 and two electives. The graduate starts full-time work in September, takes Capstone 1 and Capstone 2 with the CPA body the next summer, and writes the CFE that September. N4U4U7ON17

Time off around Capstone 2 and the CFE is arranged with the employer; CPAWSB notes the program assumes only the few days between Capstone 2 and the CFE. One university says Capstone 1, Capstone 2 and the CFE can be completed in five months. W32U16

Master’s program covering all six modules

Longer master’s programs include both Capstones, so graduates go straight to the CFE. In the West the two accredited master’s programs run over two summers, with work in between; Waterloo’s MAcc took eight months. N4U34X1U2

CPA PEP part time while working

The route with no university program: one module per session alongside a full-time job. Most candidates finish the six modules in 16 to 24 months. W29W25

University graduate program in Quebec

A DESS replaces all six modules; HEC’s current program is a 16-month cohort. Students fit a work term inside the program and write the CFE in September. Quebec requires 24 months of experience. N4QC21QC18QC9

blocks.stepAll:
All 7 steps

Step 1 · Before you start

Entry: degree, credits, and proof of accounting knowledge

  • A degree (or equivalent), at least 120 credit hours, a minimum GPA set by the region, and evidence of good character. ON9W2A2
  • Accounting and business knowledge is shown one of two ways: recognized post-secondary coursework, or passing the Knowledge Assessment. N2ON9W3
  • Knowledge Assessment: 150 objective-format questions in 5 hours. Part A is 3 hours (90 questions across eight topic areas), Part B is 2 hours (60 questions, half Financial Reporting and half Management Decision-Making). No reference materials. To pass you need sufficiency on Financial Reporting, on Management Decision-Making, and overall. N1
  • Offered three times a year. First sitting: March 23, 2027. ON4W7W4
OntarioMinimum 70% GPA across the 120 credit hours. Knowledge is shown by the 15 CPA Qualifying Courses (7 named + 8 other business courses) or the Knowledge Assessment, completed within three years before enrolling in Foundational Development. Up to three Knowledge Assessment attempts. Non-degree route: eight years of relevant experience. ON9ON10ON11ON12
QuebecA bachelor’s degree recognized by the Order (or the equivalence process), obtained within the five years before applying. No minimum average for the program delivered by the Order; universities set their own. QC1
WestMinimum 65% GPA on the most recent 60 credit hours. Knowledge is 45 credit hours (21 in required topics + 24 other) or the Knowledge Assessment; currency window is five years. Non-degree applicants can use an eight-year “advanced experience” pathway. W2W11
AtlanticMinimum 65% GPA. Same 45-credit-hour rule (21 + 24) with one course inside five years, or the Knowledge Assessment (result valid five years). A2A6A3
Step 2 · Module 1

Module 1: Foundational Development

  • Develops the Specific, Foundational and Sub-Foundational Competencies and begins the CPA Advanced Professional Competencies. Experience reporting can begin when this module starts. N2W5
  • You must pass the module’s own assessments before you can sit its exam. W5ON2
  • Foundational Development Exam: 5 hours. 50 objective-format questions (33%) plus 4 to 8 testlets (67%). Pass requires sufficiency on Financial Reporting and Management Decision-Making combined, and overall. Handbooks, Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act available. Non-disclosed. N1
  • This is the only module exam that is not part of the three-part Professional Final Exam. W6W16
Ontario14 weeks, delivered by accredited universities, not CPA Ontario: online through Executive Education at Rotman, Waterloo or Ivey (self-paced, minimum 15 hours a week), or in-person in a graduate program. First online offering May 31, 2027. Accredited in-person programs may deliver their own equivalent of the module exam. ON2ON13
Quebec16 weeks + 2 weeks of exam preparation, online in the Order’s program; or equivalent university courses. Order modules begin May 2027. The exam is run by the universities for graduate-program candidates and by the Order for its own candidates. QC3QC1
WestOnline, weekly submissions, with a two-day in-person orientation workshop. Standard track (about 20 h/week) or flexible track (about 10 h/week). First start May 15, 2027; registration opens Feb 1, 2027. Module $2,000, exam $1,000. W5W7W8
AtlanticSame design and dates as the West: first start May 15, 2027, registration from January 2027. The schedule lists the two-day orientation workshop as online. Module $2,000, exam $1,000. A2
Step 3 · Module 2

Module 2: CPA Core, in a Common or a Licensure version

  • CPA Core – Common builds financial reporting, assurance and trust, big data and analytics, and tax. CPA Core – Licensure contains all of Common plus more depth, and is required for anyone who wants a public accounting licence. N2W5ON1
  • Professional Final Exam 1, Common: two to three cases of 60 to 120 minutes each, 3 hours in total. N1
  • Professional Final Exam 1, Licensure: Part A is the same cases as the Common exam (3 hours); Part B is one 2-hour licensure case. Passing needs overall sufficiency and “readiness for licensure” on Part B. N1
  • A candidate who passes only Part A still progresses in the program; a separate licensure exam can be written after certification. N1
OntarioCommon 8 weeks (first online offering Jul 12, 2027); Licensure 14 weeks (first online offering May 31, 2027). ON2
QuebecThe licensure version is called “Core – Common + Public accountancy” and leads to the CPA auditor designation. Common 8 weeks + 2; Common + Public accountancy 14 weeks + 2. QC3QC1
WestLicensure first starts May 29, 2027, Common Jul 10, 2027; both lead to the Sep 16, 2027 exam. Either module $1,600; exam $1,350. W7W8
AtlanticSame start dates as the West (May 29 and Jul 10, 2027). Either module $1,600; exam $1,350. A2
Step 4 · Module 3

Module 3: CPA Leadership

  • Applies the decision process to real-world challenges that integrate every topic area; the focus is critical thinking and the CPA Ethical Mindset. N2
  • Professional Final Exam 2: one 5-hour comprehensive case of moderate complexity, with limited direction and designed to be time-pressured. This is the only disclosed exam in the program. N1
  • Heaviest content areas on the exam: Strategy, Risk Management and Innovation (20–35%), Ethical Decision-Making and Governance (15–30%), Management Decision-Making (15–30%). N1
Ontario10 weeks; first online offering Jun 28, 2027. Exam 1 may be written before or after this module. ON2ON13
Quebec10 weeks + 2 weeks of exam preparation, online. Each exam must be passed before moving to the next module. QC3QC2
WestFirst start Jun 26, 2027. Learners may take Leadership before writing Exam 1, but on a first attempt Exam 1 must be written before or together with Exam 2. Module $2,000; exam $1,400. W7W11W8
AtlanticFirst start Jun 26, 2027. Module $2,000; exam $1,400. A2
Step 5 · Checkpoint

Checkpoint: experience must be finished before the last module

  • Every region requires all experience requirements to be met before a learner can register for CPA Professional Readiness. This is the main structural change from the current program. ON1W5A1QC2
  • 24 months of qualifying experience, net of leaves: up to 8 months of Foundational experience and at least 16 months of Professional experience. ON5W9A1QC6
  • Professional experience needs a CPA mentor and an experience (work) plan approved by the provincial body before it starts to count. ON5W11QC6
OntarioFoundational experience can date from up to five years before Foundational Development; all 24 months can be Professional if the role is already at that level. Full-time is 35 hours a week. ON5ON12
QuebecExperience must be completed and recognized by the Order. Full-time is at least 32 hours a week; the Order checks only a work plan at the start and a report at the end. QC2QC6
WestExams 1 and 2 must also be passed. Full-time equivalent is 35 hours a week. Organizations can hold “pre-reviewed” experience plans. W11
AtlanticExams 1 and 2 and all practical experience must be complete before the module. CPA ASB approves the work plan. A1A7
Step 6 · Module 4

Module 4: CPA Professional Readiness

  • Self-study plus a five-day, in-person, case-based experience covering the code of conduct, teamwork, and emerging global, social and technological issues. W5ON1N2
  • Professional Final Exam 3: one 2-hour professional-judgment case and one 1-hour ethical decision-making case. Each case is marked holistically and both must be passed. Not designed to be time-pressured. N1
  • After passing Exam 3 the learner applies for membership in their province. W5A1
OntarioDelivered by CPA Ontario itself, five days in person. The first module “takes place in winter 2028”; first Exam 3 is Jan 20, 2028. No exemptions from this module. ON2ON4ON13
QuebecDelivered only by the Order, for both pathways: 5 days in person plus 2 weeks of online preparation. QC3QC5
WestFirst offering starts Dec 11, 2027 with the in-person workshop Dec 13–17, 2027; Exam 3 on Jan 20, 2028. Module $1,800; exam $1,400. W7W8
AtlanticSame first offering: starts Dec 11, 2027, workshop Dec 13–17, 2027. Module $1,800; exam $1,400. A2
Step 7 · Finish

Membership

  • The designation and its legal recognition do not change; graduates of the new program receive the same CPA designation. QC1
  • Public accounting licensure is applied for after membership and requires the Licensure version of CPA Core and Exam 1 plus the licensure experience. W11ON1
OntarioLicensure pathway: all 24 months in an External Audit Training Office, with at least 2,500 chargeable hours including 1,250 in assurance (625 audit). ON15ON5
QuebecCPA auditor: 24 months at an audit firm including 1,250 assurance hours, 625 of them auditing general-purpose financial statements. QC1
WestAudit: 1,250 chargeable assurance hours, at least 625 in audit. Review: 1,250, at least 625 in audit or review. Compilation: 625. W11
AtlanticLicensure experience needs a Licensed Public Accountant as mentor and a firm registered for public accounting; “applicable chargeable hours” are set provincially. A7

blocks.cards:
Ontario

CPA Ontario
  • Universities teach the first three modules and set their fees. Online through Rotman, Waterloo or Ivey Executive Education, or in person in an accredited graduate program. ON2ON12
  • Highest academic bar: 70% GPA over 120 credit hours, and qualifying courses no more than three years old. ON9
  • Transition is automatic. CPA Ontario moves students across on fixed cut-off dates from July 15, 2027; registration by Dec 31, 2026 is needed to stay on the current CFE route. ON14ON6
  • Rules are final, prices are not. Regulations 9-3 and 9-4 took effect Nov 1, 2026, but no exam or module fees were published. ON13ON4

Quebec

Ordre des CPA du Québec
  • Two pathways: the Order’s online program or a graduate program at one of 11 universities; both end with the Order’s Professional Readiness module. QC2QC5
  • No minimum average for the Order’s program; the degree must be recent (five years). QC1
  • Strictly sequential: pass each exam before the next module. The Module 1 exam is run by the universities for their own students. QC2QC1
  • Practical experience was already 24 months in Quebec; what changes is the Foundational / Professional split and lighter monitoring. QC9QC6

West and the territories

CPAWSB with CPABC, CPA Alberta, CPA Saskatchewan, CPA Manitoba, CPA Yukon, CPA NWT/Nunavut
  • Most complete rulebook so far: full fee schedule, dated module and exam calendar to September 2028, and published policies. W8W7W11
  • Standard or flexible pace (about 20 or 10 hours a week), with a two-day in-person orientation. W5W11
  • 65% GPA on the last 60 credits; eight-year experience route for applicants without a degree. W11
  • Shorter extension on transition: up to two extra years rather than three. One policy set and fee schedule covers all four provinces and the territories. W12W11

Atlantic and Bermuda

CPA Atlantic School of Business with CPA NS, NB, NL, PEI and Bermuda
  • Same calendar and module fees as the West; first modules May 15, 2027, registration from January 2027. A2
  • Only region with an official total: about $16,800 + HST for the program over 2.5 years, including a $500 one-time registration fee. A2
  • The school handles experience too: CPA ASB approves work plans and transition requests, rather than each provincial body. A7A4
  • Up to three extra years on transition; preparatory course registration closes Oct 20, 2027. A3A1

blocks.paths:
In-person graduate program in the summer, then a firm

The Ontario diploma model. A 12 to 14-week accredited program delivers Foundational Development, CPA Core and CPA Leadership with the university’s own module exam. The graduate writes Exams 1 and 2 at the September sitting, starts work, and returns for the five-day Professional Readiness module once 24 months of experience are recognized. ON13U4U8U23

If up to eight months of earlier co-op counts as Foundational experience, the 24 months finish sooner and Exam 3 moves up one or two sittings. Not every program follows this shape: Guelph’s master’s places Exam 1 in September and Exam 2 in January. ON5U1U26

Modules part time while working

The route with no graduate program: through the regional school in the West and Atlantic, online through a partner university in Ontario, or through the Order in Quebec. One module leads to each exam sitting. W7A2ON2QC2

Dates follow the western regular-track calendar. In Ontario the three modules on this route are delivered online by a university rather than by the CPA body. W7ON2

University graduate program in Quebec

HEC Montréal’s published sequence: courses in summer and fall, Exam 1 in January, a winter work term, CPA Leadership the next summer and Exam 2 in September. Professional Readiness and Exam 3 follow with the Order once 24 months are recognized. QC13QC3

Master’s over two summers (West)

The University of Saskatchewan’s published pathway: year 1 courses then Exam 1, year 2 courses then Exam 2, work in between, and Professional Readiness with Exam 3 at the end. CPAWSB had not yet published placement rules for accredited graduates. U34U35W18

blocks.openList:
“Launch” means different things. CPA Ontario says the program launches in January 2027; CPABC, CPA Saskatchewan and CPA Manitoba say May 2027. Both describe one schedule: rules, registration and the transition window start in January 2027, the first modules start in May 2027 and the first exams are in September 2027. ON1BC1W1W13
Ontario prices and enrolment. CPA Ontario had published no fee for the Knowledge Assessment, any exam or Professional Readiness, and universities had not posted tuition for the online modules. Enrolment details were promised for late 2026. Professional Readiness dates beyond “winter 2028” are not set. ON4ON2ON12
Accreditation lists not final. Ontario’s university approvals were “anticipated in the fall”; Quebec’s lists were “subject to accreditation” in fall 2026 and four Université du Québec campuses had not posted course lists. ON2QC5
Quebec fees, rules and the Knowledge Assessment. The Order’s “Costs, policies and rules” page reads “Coming soon”; module durations are “for information purposes only”; the Order’s web pages do not say whether or how the Knowledge Assessment will be used in Quebec. QC8QC2QC1
Western policies are a draft. The Education and Experience Policies are marked “Draft published May 2026”. The sections on regional transfers, advanced placement for accredited learners and international learners read “To come”, and the Learner Guide is due in early 2027. W11
Summary pages lag the schedules. CPAWSB’s key-date lists give months (“July 2028” for the last Capstone 2) while its schedule gives Aug 5, 2028; one page says final Core 1 registration closes in early November 2026 while the schedule shows Nov 23. CPA Atlantic’s overview mentions a Core 1 offering in May 2027 where the schedule shows an exam rewrite only. Use the dated schedules. W13W15W25A1
Atlantic details that differ between pages. The program description mentions a two-day in-person orientation, but the schedule lists the May 15–16, 2027 workshop as online. The fees page names Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador and Bermuda as the bodies served and omits Prince Edward Island, which the transition policy and course lists include. A2A5
Sample exams may be revised. Sample cases “have not undergone the full range of processes and quality assurance checks”; corrected versions and full Knowledge Assessment and Foundational Development sample exams are due in early 2027. ON3W6
Western accredited master’s programs. CPAWSB says the University of Alberta MAcc and the University of Saskatchewan MPAcc will continue with advanced placement, but its policy section on accredited learners still reads “To come”. The University of Alberta says it “will not proceed with a new Master of Accounting intake in Spring 2027”. Saskatchewan’s brochure says students are exempt from the Foundational Development module and exam; no CPAWSB document confirms this or says which version of Exam 1 applies. W18W11X1U35 includes a non-CPA source
Who examines Ontario graduate-program students at the first stage. Regulation 9-3 exempts in-person graduates from the Foundational Development exam and lets an accredited university deliver an equivalent. University pages describe this differently: some say the exam is bypassed, Waterloo’s MAcc says students “write the Foundational Development examination”, and Queen’s says the assessment is administered by the school. Pages also differ on whether a program delivers CPA Core Common, Licensure or both. ON13U4U8U1U18 includes a non-CPA source
Ontario accreditation not confirmed school by school. CPA Ontario lists 17 institutions that applied for in-person accreditation but had not published approvals. University pages range from “under review” (Western DAN, York LA&PS) to “accredited” or “has received accreditation approval” (Ivey, Laurier, Guelph, Schulich). Toronto Metropolitan’s diploma takes its final intake in winter 2027 with no replacement page found; Ottawa and Lakehead show no redesigned program; Brock’s site could not be read; Toronto Mississauga’s MMPA is paused. ON2U6U15U13U25U12 includes a non-CPA source
Quebec and Atlantic university details. The Order had not posted new-program course lists for UQTR, UQAT, UQAC and UQAR, and all Quebec lists remain subject to accreditation. In Atlantic Canada, CPA Canada’s 2023 list shows one accredited program (Saint Mary’s MBA, CPA stream), which CPA Atlantic’s site does not mention; nothing is published for the new program. QC5QC22N4U36 includes a non-CPA source
The national list of accredited programs is a 2023 snapshot. CPA Canada’s list of which CPA PEP modules each university program covers could only be read as a September 2023 copy from the Internet Archive. Programs have changed since (for example, Toronto Metropolitan was still listed as Ryerson). CPAWSB’s CFE page also lists Capstone 2 as a separate requirement, while the list shows the western master’s programs covering it. N4W21
